title: Return and Disposal of Medications
canonicalText:
[[PA.5203 | Return and Disposal of Medications | Applies to: PACE | Revised 02/01/2025]]
<<page 1>>
I. PURPOSE
This policy outlines the standards and procedures for the proper return and disposal of medications,
including review of such returns and disposals, by the CalOptima Health Program of All-Inclusive Care
for the Elderly (PACE) Center.
II. POLICY
A. CalOptima Health PACE shall promote timely, accurate, and documented return and disposal of
  medications.
B. The CalOptima Health PACE pharmacist, clinic Registered Nurse (RN), or Licensed Vocational
  Nurse (LVN) shall conduct a monthly review of expiration dates on all CalOptima Health PACE
  clinic medications to identify expired medications for disposal.
C. CalOptima Health PACE shall retain the Drug Disposal Logs for at least ten (10) years.
III. PROCEDURE
A. Monthly medication review is recorded in the Stock Medication Log by the RN, or LVN,
  conducting the review.
B. Identifying medications for disposal
  1. The CalOptima Health PACE clinic licensed nurse shall identify medications for disposal if found
    to be:
    a. Discolored;
    b. Solutions containing inappropriate precipitates;
    c. Vials that are soiled;
    d. Expired; or
    e. Discontinued by the provider.
<<page 2>>
  2. If medication is found to be in any of the states described in Section III.B.1 of this Policy, the
    medication will be destroyed immediately, in accordance with Section III.E of this Policy.
  3. If there is evidence of medication tampering (seal broken from unknown cause or missing
    medications), the CalOptima Health PACE nurse shall:
    a. Call the appropriate pharmacy and communicate the incident;
    b. Return immediately all medications along with the medication vial, bubble pack, or pill
      bottle to the dispensing pharmacy for review;
    c. Notify the appropriate team members of tampering incident; and
    d. Follow-up with the pharmacy to update and relay findings for review.
  4. Multiple dose vials are dated upon opening and initials of the employee opening the vials must be
    noted.
  5. Unless the manufacturer states otherwise, the CalOptima Health PACE RN or LVN shall discard
    multiple dose vials within twenty-eight (28) days after opening.
    B. CalOptima Health PACE shall contact the contracted pharmacist or the CalOptima Health PACE
    Pharmacist for guidance if there are any questions.
C. Discontinued medications from Participant supply
  1. CalOptima Health PACE shall:
    a. Prohibit the transfer of a medication to any Participant other than for whom it was
      prescribed in accordance with federal law;
    b. Remove discontinued medications from the Participant’s medication supply and dispose of
      the medication in accordance with state and federal regulations; and
    c. Not use discontinued medication for other Participants.
  2. Non-returnable medication that has been left in the CalOptima Health PACE Center by
    Participants, who are not expected to return, shall be destroyed in accordance with this Policy.
D. Expired Medications from Participant Supply
  1. The CalOptima Health PACE RN or LVN, shall identify medications that are expired.
  2. The clinic RN or LVN shall remove expired or outdated medication from the Participant’s
    medication supply and log the disposal of the medications in the Drug Disposal Log.
      i. The medication must be destroyed, in accordance with state and federal regulations.
E. Medication Destruction Procedures
  1. Controlled Substances
    a. CalOptima Health PACE shall keep a log of all destroyed Controlled Substances using the
      CalOptima Health PACE Controlled Substance Disposal Log.
<<page 3>>
      i. Two (2) CalOptima Health PACE licensed nurses shall document the drug destructions
        and sign their names on the CalOptima Health PACE Drug Disposal Log.
    b. All Controlled Substances to be destroyed shall be stored in a double-locked storage
      system, designated in the CalOptima Health PACE Center for disposed Controlled
      Substances.
    c. The double-locked storage system shall be a separate storage system from Controlled
      Substances still in use.
    d. Controlled Substances shall be subject to the CalOptima Health Policy PA.5202: Labeling
      and Clinic Storage of Medications.
  2. Non-Controlled Substances
    a. CalOptima Health PACE shall keep a log of all destroyed non-Controlled Substances using
      the CalOptima Health PACE Drug Disposal Log.
    b. Non-Controlled Substances will be destroyed on-site by one (1) CalOptima Health PACE
      licensed nurse and one (1) clinic employee.
  3. Disposal of drugs
    a. CalOptima Health PACE shall place all non-sealed drugs for disposal into the
      “pharmaceutical waste” container in the clinic.
    b. Medication labels will be removed or obscured using a black permanent marker prior to
      disposal.
    c. The bio-hazardous waste vendor will pick up these containers on a regular scheduled basis
      and incinerate the contents.
F. Monitoring of return and disposal medication
  1. The CalOptima Health PACE Pharmacist shall:
    a. Conduct frequent reviews and update the CalOptima Health PACE Quality Improvement
      department with any quality issues as needed; and
    b. Work with the CalOptima Health PACE contracted pharmacies on any needed Corrective
      Action Plan (CAP).
V. REFERENCE(S)
A. CalOptima Health PACE Contract with the Department of Health Care Services for the PACE
  Program
B. CalOptima Health Policy PA.5202: Labeling and Clinic Storage of Medications
<<page 4>>
C. CalOptima Health PACE Program Agreement
D. Title 22, California Code of Regulations (C.C.R.), §78317
E. Title 42, Code of Federal Regulations (C.F.R.), §423.505(e)(4)
<<page 5>>
IX. GLOSSARY
Controlled Substance: A drug or other substance, or immediate precursor included in Schedule I, II, III, IV, or V of the Federal Controlled Substances Act.
PACE Center: The location designated by CalOptima Health PACE at which Participants shall receive PCP services.
Participant: An individual enrolled in the CalOptima Health PACE program.
